title: Multi-cloud and hybrid: the seams between providers, where control is thinnest

videos.script: A company on two providers has three things to defend. {{three}} Each side, and the join between them. The join belongs to neither side's tools, so that is where control is thinnest. {{four}} Four things cross it. An identity, a route, a record and a policy. {{key}} This lesson follows the identity first, because it hurts most often. An access key is created in AWS and pasted into a job in Google Cloud. It works on the first try. It never expires. And nobody on either side owns it. {{audit}} You will find it the way an auditor would, from the credential report and the key's last use. {{token}} Then you replace it. The job proves who it is with a token its own provider signs. AWS trades that token for credentials that expire within the hour. {{retire}} Nothing is left on either side that would still work next week. {{links}} The lesson ends with the links between networks, and the inside that grows when two of them meet. {{end}}
